public_rationale: In the disclosures around the post, no major hyperscaler reported actual dollar revenue from renting GPUs or its own chips. Oracle gave only a growth rate: 'GPU-related revenue growing 177%'. Microsoft had never even given Azure revenue in dollars before October 2026. Amazon came closest. It said its chips business, Trainium plus the Graviton CPU, was over a $10bn annual run rate, and that Trainium2 was a 'multi-billion dollar' run-rate business. Those are annualized, partly vague figures that mix CPUs and AI chips, not actual reported GPU or accelerator rental revenue. So on the plain reading the factual claim holds. His explanation for why they don't disclose is opinion and is not scored.
limitations: Amazon's run-rate figures are a partial disclosure; a reader who counts run rates as revenue would score this mixed.
Google's practice was not documented by a cited item.
Microsoft evidence comes from a later news report describing past practice.
